messages:
Liam: Heads-up — ClearWave renewal in 30d. They want to drop committed GPUs from 40 -> 20 but keep Private deployment and existing SLA. Can we do a mid-term commit adjustment?
Maya: Hmm, dropping commit that much usually triggers a rebaseline. Do we have usage history to justify?
Emma (CSM): They ran a 6wk POC for our reranker and adoption didn't land as expected. Usage down ~45% last quarter. Customer requests lower fixed spend but wants private + HSM.
Priya (Deal Desk): @Liam @Emma need a formal exception request. Options we usually consider: prorated reduction for remainder of term, switch to a smaller committed tier with a short extension, or convert to usage-based with a minimum. What delta on ARR if we do 20 GPUs?
Liam: Quick numbers: current committed = 40 GPUs @ $90k/mo (rate card), proposed 20 GPUs @ $50k/mo. That’s ~40% monthly revenue drop. They offered a 12mo extension to keep unit price, but want immediate cut now.
Jared (Solutions): Two technical blockers: 1) Private deploy + HSM is an add-on that we price separately (~+20% uplift on committed fees). 2) Reducing infra footprint mid-term affects reserved pool allocation — we need Eng sign-off to shift capacity.
sec-bot: Security questionnaire status: ClearWave answered 78/120 items. Outstanding: key rotation policy, HSM cert chain, and SOC2 evidence. ETA from Sec team: 4 business days for final review.
Maya: Given the HSM ask, the +20% should be non-negotiable. If they reduce commit and keep HSM, net ARR impact is less severe. Suggest we model three scenarios and present to customer.
Priya (Deal Desk): Agreed. I’ll prepare a rate card exception packet but need: 1) justification (usage drop + POC notes), 2) proposed term change, 3) legal/finance impact statement. Who can compile?
Emma (CSM): I’ll attach the POC summary and usage dashboard. Also will get a note from the account team about future roadmap adoption that might restore usage.
Liam: I can draft the customer email with 3 options:
• Option A — Short-term reduction: 20 GPUs for remaining 6 months, prorated, +20% HSM surcharge, no extension.
• Option B — Reduce to 20 GPUs, but extend term 12 months at current committed unit price (with HSM surcharge).
• Option C — Move to usage-based billing with a guaranteed monthly floor equal to 80% of proposed 20 GPU commit for 12 months.
Priya (Deal Desk): Provide ARR delta for each. For approvals: need Deal Desk + Head of Rev Ops signoff for >25% ARR change. Legal to review T&Cs for mid-term amend.
Jared (Solutions): FYI — if they go to Option B we must reserve capacity for their new smaller pool; Eng needs 72h lead time to reconfigure. Also confirm HSM supplier and cert timeline.
Maya: Also flag: rate-card rule #7 — mid-term commit reductions under 50% require CFO approval if customer keeps SLA.
Liam: Understood. I'll run modeling and put numbers in the exception form.
Priya (Deal Desk): Please attach: usage CSV, POC notes, security status, and the proposed customer email. I’ll open the deal-desk ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/DD-2345 — add comments there.
Emma (CSM): I pinged the customer repo with the POC report and asked them to confirm whether they can commit to the 12mo extension if we offer Option B. They replied: "we prefer Option C but could consider B with higher visibility into roadmap".
sec-bot: Added sec summary to ticket DD-2345; pending items assigned to @Jared.
Priya (Deal Desk): Timeline: I’ll intake today; aim to present to Rev Ops and CFO by EOD tomorrow. If anyone has objections to the +20% HSM surcharge being mandatory, flag now.
Maya: No objections from me.
Jared (Solutions): No objections — but need clarity on HSM vendor and certs to finalize pricing.
Liam: Ok team — I’ll assemble materials and drop in DD-2345 before noon. Thanks :thumbsup:
